name: Reduce Story opening latency from Find Stories
description:
Opening a Story from Find Stories intermittently waits for seconds. Investigation found coordination overhead and optional Plugin content on the critical path; fuzzy matching itself took 2.66 ms for 70 Stories.

Measured details loading uses 11 separate coordinated acquisitions (22 fsynced lock temporary files). A controlled 2 s Git publication-gate hold made a Story read take 2.004 s. Injecting 50 ms per lock write made details take 1.207 s; the same reads in one coordinated snapshot took 123 ms. Quiet baseline details took 15–16 ms, so the original intermittent incident still needs lock-wait telemetry for conclusive attribution.

Fix: instrument lock wait versus held work; avoid same-Board context.use mutations and covered Board reloads; show core Story/config before optional rows/badges; batch bounded reads without weakening lock/recovery guarantees; reduce Story Linking full-Board scans and repeated Epic/Spec reads. Finder indexing is a related separate bottleneck: 102 acquisitions in this Data Root.

See Story Spec performance-report for the full diagnosis, measurements, source paths, fix plan and acceptance criteria. Scope is implementation of that plan with appropriate manual profiling and required regression checks. Keep same-Board/cross-Board navigation, freshness, invalid Plugin Data handling and ADR-0019 guarantees intact.

comments.author: sunny
comments.body:
ROW-72 API ADDENDUM ACCEPTED for implementation, with the following binding clarifications. This completes plan acceptance for the remaining scope; continue the same worker/worktree.

The ordered discriminated results, missing-file behavior, duplicate handling, validation before acquisition, unchanged single-read APIs, bounded request batches, separate existing Finder inventory calls, and fresh per-build search loader are accepted. No Plugin callback runs under the Data Root lock. Keep existing inventory atomicity; no outer whole-Board/Data Root scope or cross-build cache.

Error classification must preserve coordination and core data integrity at every depth: publication/lock/recovery errors reject the whole call with the original error; DATA_INTEGRITY encountered while resolving a Board/Story scope also rejects the whole call, rather than being converted into a per-file failed result. Scope resolution can read core JSON, so not every error inside the entry loop is a tolerant file error. Ordinary per-file filesystem/path-policy errors and missing scope NOT_FOUND follow the documented per-entry contract. No blanket catch/retry fallback. Epics may display ordinary unreadable entries but must propagate acquisition/core-integrity failures to its existing caller boundary. Finder may omit that Plugin's unavailable search text at the documented loader boundary without retrying or hiding Stories.

Document the listMany 256-name threshold as a soft stopping threshold evaluated after a complete scope, not a hard maximum on names, filesystem calls or time. One scope may exceed it. The 32-entry read limit likewise does not bound scope-resolution I/O/time. Preserve the FIFO release/reacquire behavior between batches and make no stronger fairness claim than the actual coordinator guarantees.

Extend existing required storage/Plugin contract test homes without increasing the suite beyond 100. In addition to the planned publication/recovery assertion, cover representative ordered/missing/per-entry failure results and whole-call failure classification (including corrupt core scope resolution), plus a deterministic inter-batch queued-mutation barrier if the existing checks do not already establish the claimed release/fairness behavior. These are contract/pipeline/race checks, not exhaustive per-input tests. Compiled API documentation fixtures must cover the public types and loader. Maintain existing tests and full four-check validation.

ADR-0052 is provisionally reserved for this Story, subject to your fresh collision check across origin/main and active PRs before writing/publishing; ROW-69's 0051 reservation remains separate. Do not reverse an accepted ADR. Include all relevant API/storage/operation/user-guide/skill reference documentation updates where behavior changed.

You may capture final agentic-tui evidence after the API portion; no separate interim screenshot run is required. Use the already reported private state directory and preserve linked evidence. Report the exact location/type/ownership of the pristine baseline archive/copy and any other new comparison resources in your handoff; retain them, with no production cleanup assumed.

Keep measurements phase-specific: the reported core improvement does not imply enrichment/Finder index improved. Provide the complete before/after 71/501, Plugins on/off, quiet/synthetic-lock-cost results and I/O-counting limits, plus original-cause uncertainty. If remaining measured Finder cost warrants caching beyond this accepted design, stop and report before adding it. Canonical selection absence remains audited, not backfilled.

ROW-72 round 2: PARTIAL PLAN ACCEPTANCE.

You may implement the independent portion now in the existing worktree: opt-in coordination telemetry (operation names and durations only), same-context-Board selection without context.use/version changes with route reset decided separately, core Story/config loading before optional enrichment, freshness guards and usable keys/hints, and the one deterministic TUI barrier regression you proposed. Keep optional Plugin callbacks outside the Data Root lock. Update the corresponding docs and measure these phases. The existing publication/recovery test can cover telemetry now; extend it for batch reads only after the API contract is accepted. The total remains at most 100 tests. Your private agentic-tui state directory ownership is recorded; you may use it for this accepted scope under the existing screenshot/check rules.

The new files.readMany/listMany, loadStorySearchText, associated Plugin migrations and Finder inventory batching are NOT accepted for implementation yet. Before coding that portion, send a short typed interface/semantics addendum:
1. Exact input/result types, ordered association to requested entries/scopes, missing-file behavior, duplicate handling, validation, and error semantics across multiple batches. "An I/O error rejects only its own batch" does not yet define the caller's observable result. Distinguish tolerant per-file display errors from publication/lock/recovery/data-integrity failures. A generic catch-and-retry-every-file fallback must not swallow or repeatedly retry coordination/integrity failures.
2. Remove the proposed single outer scope across boards.list + stories.list + every Board config: that can cover the whole Data Root and contradicts the stated bound. Explain the bounded inventory approach while retaining the existing service consistency guarantees. Distinguish 32 requested entries/scopes from 32 filesystem operations or bounded time: recursive list and stories.list may each read arbitrarily many files. Do not claim the latter bounds without evidence or change existing atomic service semantics silently.
3. Confirm the search loader's failure handling, freshness/invalidation and compatibility with existing storySearchText callbacks; no callbacks under the lock and no unbounded whole-Board/Root wrapper.

This is an interface/implementation clarification within the existing Story, not a request to expand scope or reverse ADR-0019. A new ADR must use docs/agents/adr and the index; ROW-69 has a pending reservation for 0051, so coordinate a different free number. Your before/after measurement plan and conditional cache deferral are accepted as evidence requirements, not promised performance results. Keep reporting mechanisms separately from the unproved original incident cause.

Canonical Model Selection absence remains audited by Comment SmCEMgSY and the verified receipt; do not backfill it, restart or duplicate this worker. Report progress and the API addendum here; await separate acceptance before that API portion.

comments.body: Review of https://github.com/sgolovine/rowbly/pull/153 at 472ec7bcb51a310cee6f9ee6422696edbb2013a8 by codex/gpt-6-astra: CHANGES REQUESTED. 1. [P2] Preserve elapsed phase timing when acquisition fails (src/services/coordination.ts:160-170; src/storage/lock.ts:141-146). Phase durations are assigned only after successful awaits. A publication timeout never calls published(), a queue timeout never records queuedMs, and a lock-file timeout never records waitedMs; recovery failures similarly omit their duration. In an isolated Git fixture, a real publication-gate timeout took 10003.7 ms but emitted wait=publication:0.0,queue:0.0,lock:0.0,recovery:0.0 and held 0.0 ms. This erases the diagnostic evidence for the slowest failed openings. Finalize the active phase on rejection as well as success, preserve the original error and privacy restrictions, and extend the existing telemetry regression to cover a failed acquisition without brittle timing thresholds. 2. [P2] Isolate search-loader inputs from the core index (src/tui/shell/storySearch.ts:29-35). Every loader receives the same mutable array and Story objects that core subsequently indexes. The readonly array type does not make Story fields immutable. A loader that assigns stories[0].name and then throws leaves that modified name in the index, so the original core name no longer matches; a JavaScript loader that splices the array and throws removes Stories entirely. Both were reproduced against this head. The failure catch cannot restore the inventory, contrary to the accepted detached-input and failure-isolation requirement. Give loaders isolated snapshots, keep the core inventory private, and protect the returned per-Story mapper boundary too.
